prompt: Stage 5-2, level 8, 47 gold, 30 HP, five players left. Your rolldown at 5-1 hit: Sivir and Sentinel are 2-star with their items and every unit on the board is 2-star. Seats 1 and 3 are level 9 with capped boards you lose to badly; Seat 4 beat you by two units and sits at 24 HP; Seat 7 is at 12 HP and loses to everyone. You hold two spare Tristana. Level 9 is 52 XP away. What do you do with the 47 gold?

lobby.note: Level 9, 2-star Ashe with three items and two 5-costs; you lose badly
Level 9, capped Coven with 2-star Kennen; you lose
2-star Ezreal and a 2-star Tristana; beat you by two units at 5-1
1-star board; loses to everyone, including you

options.label: Stop rolling. Bank this round, level 9 at 5-3 with gold left over, and roll there for Ashe or Elder Dragon
Roll to 10 now at level 8 for a 5-cost or any 2-star upgrade; every fight matters at 30 HP
Roll 20 for the Tristana 3-star: you hold four and she is the cheapest upgrade on the board
Roll to 0 now: 30 HP is under the two-losses line at stage 5, so stabilise

explanation:
Your board at 8 is finished; only a 5-cost moves it. At level 8 a slot is a 5-cost 3% of the time; with roughly 80 five-cost copies left and 15 of them Ashe or Elder Dragon, that is 0.6% per slot, 3% per shop, and 18 shops find one about 40% of the time, and then it must replace a unit. At level 9 the same targets are 13% per shop: ten shops find one three times in four and it joins the board as a ninth unit. Banking puts you at 56 at 5-3, level 9 costs 52, and you roll from there at the right odds.

Seat 7 dies on his next loss, which locks top 4; 3rd is a race with Seat 4 at 24 HP where both of you lose to the top two. The two-losses rule is about turning losses into wins, and no roll at 8 turns a loss to Seat 1 or 3 into anything. Tristana 3-star is arithmetic: Seat 4 holds three, you hold four, eleven remain, and 18 shops at 1.5% a slot produce about one copy, not five.
principle: When 4th is locked and the boards above you are out of reach at 8, gold is for level 9, not for shops at the wrong odds.
commonMistake: Rolling at level 8 on a finished board because 'every fight matters', when nothing at 8 changes the fights you lose.
hint: List the upgrades that could still change a fight against the boards above you, and check the odds of each at level 8 versus 9.
